ac.description: The switch as shipped: one 920 W AC supply in slot 0, a cover panel over slot 1 and two front-to-back fan modules, all marked AIR OUT. A second supply raises the PoE budget from 740 W to 1440 W.

description: Juniper EX4100-24P, a 1U access switch with 24 10/100/1000BASE-T ports that all supply PoE+ (30 W by default). The front also has four SFP28 Virtual Chassis ports, four SFP+ uplink ports and an RS232 to USB Type-C console port. The rear has an RJ-45 management port, an RJ-45 console port, a USB 2.0 Type-A port, two fan modules and two power supply slots. It ships with one 920 W AC supply, and a cover panel closes the second slot. Airflow is front to back.

chassis.note: Table 8 and Table 19 - height 1.72 in (4.37 cm), depth 13.78 in (35 cm) with no power supply and fan module and 15.05 in (38.24 cm) with them installed, width 17.36 in (44.09 cm) with the power supply and fan module installed and for all models (Table 19 note). Table 8 also prints 15.05 in for the depth with no power supply, a misprint that Table 19 corrects, and prints 38.24 cm against 15.05 in (382.3 mm), which differ by 0.1 mm. The depth carried is the 350.0 mm of the bare chassis, and the modules add the rest, as for the EX3400. The body of 440.9 mm is the metal between the bracket fold lines. Weight is 6315 g with the supply and fan modules (Table 8) and 12.15 lb (5.51 kg) in Table 19; the two differ by 0.8 kg and Table 19 is carried because it is the table of chassis weights.

color.note: estimated - median of the bare face between the logo and the first jack block in Figure 1, #9397a0, and of the status panel, #434c59. Sampled from the guide's render, which may not match the metal.

drawing-vs-photo.note: No photograph of the real device is held. The guide's renders (Figures 1 and 2) are used for what is printed and where, and the line drawings (Figures 3 and 4) for the callouts. The renders print the port numbers in a salmon red on this PoE model (#ff8074, the median of the most saturated pixels) and in light grey on the non-PoE models; the line drawings print them black. The render wins.

ears.note: Figure 50 shows the two-post front-mounting brackets that ship (EX-RMK, Table 5, supplied) fitted flush with the front, and the guide's mounting topics give a 2 in. recessed position with the 2 in. recessed front-mounting brackets of the four-post rack-mounting kit EX-4PST-RMK (Table 5, orderable). The recess is 2 in. (50.8 mm). The wall-mount kit EX-WMK (Table 5, orderable) is a third mount. The kits are not listed under kits in this slice: the guide's parts are named but not modelled as kind kit contracts, and the figures place the brackets without a measurable fold line, so only the recess has an at.

earthing.note: Table 59 and Figure 71 - a two-hole protective earthing terminal on the rear panel, with two M5 by 10 mm screws with washers, orderable separately, and a Panduit LCD8-14A-L lug or equivalent. The holes are 16.9 mm apart on the render (the lug pitch is not stated in the guide). The two tapped holes are drawn as decor and the separately ordered screws are not drawn.

fru-bays.note: Table 7 and Table 53 - the switch ships with two fan modules and one 920 W AC supply, preinstalled. The supplies are fully redundant, load sharing and hot-removable and hot-insertable when the second supply is installed and running. The fan modules are hot-removable and hot-insertable and one is removed at a time. Do not mix AC and DC supplies, or supplies and fans of different airflow. Both supplies and fans are bays here; nothing in the chassis is built in. Transceivers are the third kind of FRU the guide names.

port-lamps.note: Figures 29 to 31 and Table 24 - each RJ-45 jack has a Link Activity lamp at one corner and a Status lamp at the other; the common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 housing carries both. Each SFP28 and SFP+ port has a Link Activity lamp and a Status lamp, drawn as arrows in the band between the two cage rows. Figure 30 numbers them 1, 1, 2, 2 across a column: down arrow, up arrow, down arrow, up arrow, so the down arrows belong to the lower port and the up arrows to the upper one. The pitch of the arrows within a column is read off Figure 1. The Status lamp's colour shows speed (Table 25), so its states are not expressible as one vocabulary here (see gaps).

port-numbering.note: Figures 1 and 3 print 0 and 1, 2 and 3, up to 22 and 23 under the column pairs, with an up triangle after the even number and a down triangle before the odd one, so the upper jack of a column is the even port. The cages are printed 0 to 3 under each block the same way, and the uplink block is bracketed and labelled UPLINK. Table 64 names the PIC numbers - 0 for the RJ-45 ports, 1 for the SFP28 ports and 2 for the SFP+ uplink ports - and the interface names (ge-0/0/n and so on) are not printed on the metal and are not stated, so none is recorded.

ports.note: estimated - Figure 3 callout 2 and Figure 1 give 24 RJ-45 ports in two blocks of two rows, the first of four columns and the second of eight. Cavity edges were found along a pixel row of Figure 1. The second block has the registry's 13.97 mm ganged pitch (measured 14.0). The first block is spread wider, 15.78 mm between columns (46.7 px), with the same jack size; the maker's line drawing (Figure 3, g022674) shows the same wider spread. Both blocks have two rows 14.31 mm apart (cavity centres 15.8 and 30.1 mm down) with the upper row turned 180 so that its lamp tabs face up, as rendered. The four SFP28 cages at 359.7 mm and the four SFP+ cages at 391.0 mm abut on the registry's 14.25 mm pitch, in two stacked rows on the jack rows' centres, the lower row turned 180 so that both lips face the band between them.

power.note: Table 32 - the EX4100-24P offers a 93 W system budget and 740 W of PoE with one 920 W supply (833 W in all), and 1440 W of PoE with two (1533 W in all of 1840 W). The guide gives no maximum power consumption for the switch, and its datasheet did not answer, so none is stated and the module power warning stands.

rear.note: estimated - Figure 2 and Figure 4. From the left, a lighter plate holds the MGMT RJ-45 over a USB 2.0 Type-A port in one housing, and the CON RJ-45. Then come fan 0 and fan 1, each with a fan icon, its number and a round status lamp to its left, a plate with the earthing terminal (two holes on a lighter strip, with the earth symbol), the ESD point and two label areas (the CLEI code and the serial number), and power supply slots 0 and 1, each with a power icon and its number to its left. Measured at 2.957 px/mm from the 441.0 mm body. The 24-port models have no claim code label on the rear; Figure 3 callout 10 puts it on the front, in the lower left.

rear-modules.note: estimated - the fan faces measure 124 by 125 px, 41.9 by 42.3 mm, 49.4 mm apart (82.3 and 131.7 mm from the left). The power supply faces measure 72.4 by 40.1 mm, 83.1 mm apart. The guide's module sizes (Table 20 note) are used for the bays (73.0 by 40.0 for a supply, 41.9 by 41.8 for a fan), centred on the measured faces. The second supply slot holds a cover panel, which the guide says to keep in an empty slot (the replacement procedures); the render shows two supplies fitted and Figure 4 shows the slot empty, so the default carries one.

scale.note: estimated - Gate 1 passed on Figure 1 (g022754), the 1500 px wide render of the EX4100-24P front. The body is 1304 px across (74 to 1378) and 129 px high, against 440.9 by 43.7 mm: aspects 10.11 and 10.09. So the figure is orthographic and is read at 2.957 px/mm. The rear render, Figure 2 (g022756), reads 2.957 px/mm the same way. The EX4100-48P front render is 0.5 percent larger (2.97 px/mm) and is measured on its own scale.

sources.note: EX4100 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks (HPE), PDF created 2026-10-01, 281 pages, fetched from juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4100/ex4100.pdf: Tables 7 and 8 (the EX4100-24P model and specifications), Table 19 (chassis), Table 20 (module sizes and weights), Tables 26 and 27 (fan modules and airflow), Tables 29 to 34 (AC supplies and the PoE budget), Figures 1 to 4 (the front and rear of the EX4100-24P), Figures 29 to 32 (the lamps) and Figures 50 to 61 (mounting). The guide is copyright Juniper Networks and Hewlett Packard Enterprise; no terms of use are printed in it. Nothing of it is copied here, since every face is drawn new from measurements. The HPE PSNow datasheet (a00150781enw) did not answer (an HTTP/2 stream error on the one try), so no datasheet figure is used and the guide is the only maker source for the numbers. Juniper's image-library paths (ex4100-24p-front-high.jpg and the rear and the same for the 24T, 48P and 48T) all returned a 404 page, so no studio photograph is held. End of life was searched on 2026-10-22 and no Juniper notice for the EX4100 was found, so the lifecycle is recorded as none announced.

status-block.note: estimated - Figure 1 and Figure 27. The four chassis lamps SYS, ALM, MST and CLD are in the left column of the dark panel at the right and the four port mode lamps SPD, DX, EN and PoE in the right column, each lamp above its legend, at 4.6 mm pitch. The Factory Reset/Mode button is a light-blue disc below them with a list symbol to its right (Figure 32), and the RS232 to USB Type-C console port, labelled CON, is below the button. Table 22 and Table 25 give the lamp meanings. The reset pinhole (callout 9) is the dot printed between ports 20 and 21.
